items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: And I'll go on record as saying that Charlie Parker influenced all the musicians

ctx.x: Well, no, and I'll tell you, I heard some music before that which, to use the expression that they use, way out. They use the expression way out, meaning if it's way out you don't know anything about it, you don't understand it, you don't like it or whatever, you say it's way out. But anyway, I always, from my training in music ever since I was very young, music is music. Of course people say but if you don't understand it it's like French. I could listen to you talk French all day. I don't know what the hell…
So that was how it came about. And I'll go on record as saying that Charlie Parker influenced all the musicians, the piano players, the bass players, the trumpet players, all

of them. Charlie Parker influenced everyone who ever played jazz, and maybe some people who didn't play jazz. Charlie Parker was a great influence in music, let's put it that way. Absolutely. And all the rest of them came after him. And there's a tremendous, tremendous amount of people still studying Charlie Parker to this day.
